searchText: <@!425279588009246720> just brought up in an issue that they believe that links to EIPs within EIPs should be absolute paths to `eips.ethereum.org/EIPs/eip-#.md`. I have been told in the past (long time ago) that they should be relative paths like `./eip-#.md`. I also believe pretty strongly that we **SHOULD** be using relative paths, as it means the page works in GitHub, forks of GitHub, the EIPs page, if the EIPs page moves, in mirrors of the EIPs page, etc. Do others have an opinion on the matter and/or is there an official stance written out somewhere (e.g., EIP-1 or something)? Hehe, glancing at EIP-1, it internally uses `[EIP-#]` which on the EIPs site renders as a link to GitHub. 😬 EIP-1 does explicitly say to use relative paths for asset links: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-1.md#eip-formats-and-templates However, it doesn't mention whether to use relative paths for other EIPs or not. Images are handled differently by Jekyll than other links. Just trying to gather available info at the moment to facilitate discussion, didn't mean to imply that that was a strong argument. Here's the context (and I added more comments there): https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2488#discussion_r479080345 <@!425279588009246720> Do you remember what the argument for absolute paths was? Generally speaking, relative paths are preferred in most web contexts (and often in desktop contexts as well), so I'm surprised that a discussion would result in absolute paths for this sort of thing as it breaks a lot. Not entirely, but one driving force was to ensure people consider the rendered version on eips.ethereum.org as the "absolute truth". As you've uncovered above, with relative links sometimes the rendered version moves people off the rendered version back to github. This may be a shortcoming in Jekyll, or the settings we use for Jekyll. Ah, so I definitely agree that eips.ethereum.org shouldn't be directing people to GitHub, but having relative paths wouldn't cause that I don't think? Let me see, I have merged some PRs recently that had relative paths, so should be easy to verify. I've spent quite a bit of time improving the Jekyll configuration in the past 2 years so maybe it is not an issue anymore, but I haven't specifically spent time on this issue. Btw, I wish the repo is kept consistent and changes like this are done at once with consensus. At the moment, Jekyll appears to do the right thing. <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2711> <https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-2711.md> Look for EIP-2718 on that page and note that it links to ethereum.org in the first and github.com in the second. Uses relative paths internally. This means I'd prefer we keep using absolute paths (including those recently merged ones), and do a once-off sweep to relative paths, if that is agreed on. > Btw, I wish the repo is kept consistent and changes like this are done at once with consensus. <@!425279588009246720> I agree with the consistency angle, which is why I wanted to discuss. I have been merging stuff with relative paths lately (and advising users on relative paths) because that is how I was trained years ago. My vote is strongly in favor of relative paths for the reasons mentioned above. **IFF** we come to consensus on that I'll do a PR that updates everything to relative paths repository wide. **IFF** we come to consensus on absolute paths, then I'll approve a PR that updates everything to absolute paths (and I'll start recommending such to authors going forward). Oh I think another reason for linking to actual EIPs with absolute path was that if someone is looking at a github fork for a given EIP, they may see an outdated version of the linked EIP. They will still see an outdated version of the EIP even if that EIP has an absolute link. Why? The absolute link goes to the official repository. I feel like the set of people who will end up on a random fork and then navigate to the latest via link and then continue browsing is a pretty small set. That is, I don't know anyone who just "browses around EIPs" like Wikipedia. Maybe there exists some set of users who do this? Are they users who are *also* likely to start off looking at some outdated fork? Some large EIPs had the tendency to link to their fork of the EIP repository for discussions. It is an edge case and not something we should be a proponent of, anyway. I'm looking through all PRs by fulldecent, I'm not seeing anything that mentions `absolute` or `relative`. Any hints on keywords for finding the previous discussion? Also tried `paths`. He used the term canonical most of the time, iirc. The initial PR: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/1192 The first URL changing PR (there are ~10 of these): https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/1730 And there's one other reason listed. Ok, I'm out for now 🙂 Ah, I found that first link (which just defined the canonical URL), but wasn't able to find the others. Thanks! I'll review them. As you can see there was a mixture of styles prior, this one changed absolute github urls: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/1808 Here's more discussion about absolute vs relative: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/1733#discussion_r261831292 https://youtu.be/y6LBpY6byd0 https://youtu.be/al4YpfDVmS4
